title: MyMood – The Rhythm of Hormones and Emotions
summary:
During the menstrual cycle, the time from one menstrual period to the next, emotions as well as mental and physical symptoms can change. The extent of these changes varies from person to person. However, little is known about why some people experience stronger fluctuations than others. In particular, it is still unclear how these changes differ between people with and without mental health conditions or those receiving different types of treatment, and to what extent these fluctuations are related to how well people recognize their own emotions and bodily signals.
The MyMood study aims to investigate how mental and physical symptoms, difficulties in everyday life, and ways of dealing with emotions change throughout the menstrual cycle. We are interested not only in whether certain symptoms occur, but also in how severe they are. We want to find out whether these changes differ between people who are not receiving psychological or psychiatric treatment, those receiving outpatient treatment, and those receiving treatment in a day hospital or psychiatric ward. We also investigate whether these changes are related to how well people recognize their own emotions and bodily signals and how they deal with their feelings.
People aged 18 years or older who understand German and have a natural menstrual cycle can take part in the study. They must not currently be pregnant, breastfeeding, or using hormonal contraception. Participation is possible regardless of whether someone has mental health problems or is receiving psychological or psychiatric treatment.
The study takes place entirely online. First, we check whether participants meet the requirements for taking part. They then receive information about the study and give their consent. Next, they complete a longer questionnaire once. After that, they answer short daily questions about their symptoms, emotions, and everyday life over two menstrual cycles (approximately 60 days).
The study does not involve any medical examinations or treatments. It does not provide medical diagnoses, treatment recommendations, or support in acute crisis situations.
conditions: menstrual cycle-associated fluctuations of mental and physical symptoms, daily functioning, and emotion regulation strategies

interventions.name:
Monocentric, non-interventional, prospective observational study with a one-time baseline assessment followed by daily assessments over two calculated menstrual cycles (approximately 60 days).

Study Population
Adults with natural menstrual cycles who are not currently using hormonal contraceptio

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Unchanged, regular menstrual bleeding over the past 6 months
Usual menstrual cycle length between 17 and 45 days
Menarche  at least 3 years ago
Self-perceived ability to cope with the psychological demands of study participation
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy or breatsfeeding within the past 3 months
Hormonal contraception within the past 3 months
